messages:
Alex R: FYI seeing a wearburst pattern on a subset of ephemeral NVMe nodes in eu-west3, GPU attaches started failing around 09:12 UTC. low-level SMART noise + huge scrub backlog.
Maya Chen: ugh, did the cleaner ramp up due to unfinished deletes?
Alex R: looks like a combination — backlog from yesterday's batch jobs + a firmware IO amplification spike. scrub concurrency peaked at 48 per host.
Samir: can we throttle the janitor? that concurrency is killing iops.
Jin Park: I can push a temporary limiter to 8 concurrent scrub workers per node. small change: reduce janitor.CONCURRENCY env var in the daemonset.
Alex R: nice. what's the rollout risk? we need to avoid starving GC on other regions.
Jin Park: low risk, will canary 10% of eu-west3 first. patch: 
```yaml
- name: JANITOR_CONCURRENCY
  value: "8"
```
Maya Chen: also can we skip deep-scrub passes for 2 hours? defer to off-peak window.
Samir: yes skip deep-scrub for ephemeral class only. we should keep light scrubs to avoid metadata blowups.
Nadia: ops-bot noticed GPU provisioning failures tied to node iowait > 85% — autoscaler is timing out attaches. fallback plan?
Alex R: plan: 1) throttle janitor concurrency 2) disable deep-scrub for ephemeral pool 3) move some batch capacity to spillover hot-pool (higher cost) 4) increase attach timeout for orchestrator by +15s as safety.
Samir: cost note — spilling to hot-pool will add ~0.6c/min per GPU for affected customers, but keeps SLA. we should notify billing if sustained.
Jin Park: canary patch ready, deploying to 3 nodes now.
ops-bot: [ALERT] eu-west3: ephemeral-nvme iowait spike detected, affected hosts: gnode-114, gnode-117, gnode-130.
Maya Chen: running quick health check, posting command outputs: 
```
# iostat -x 1 2 | egrep "gnode-114|gnode-117|gnode-130" -A2
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.20 120.00 450.00 4800 36000 72.0 5.6 8.3 1.2 9.1 2.00 96.4
```
Samir: %util 96.4 is the killer. We need to reduce write pressure. Are there sudden write bursts from checkpointing?
Alex R: yes batch jobs flushed checkpoints aggressively last night. scheduler should have smoothed but it didn't.
Nadia: I'm posting a quick incident blurb to #incidents and notifying customer success for any impacted Dedicated tenants.
Maya Chen: after throttling janitor and disabling deep-scrub, iowait dropped to ~35% on the canary nodes within 7m.
Jin Park: rolling limiter to remaining eu-west3 nodes now (30 hosts). will monitor.
ops-bot: [INFO] janitor concurrency set to 8 for ephemeral pool (rolled to 10% -> 100% in 12m).
Alex R: nice. next: we should schedule a firmware I/O amplification investigation with vendor. can't keep relying on throttle band-aids.
Samir: agree. also propose adding a short-lived rate limiter on checkpoint uploads from batch controller: `max_bytes_per_sec=50mb`
Maya Chen: logging note: add a metric `janitor.concurrent_scrubs` and alert when >20 for any host.
Nadia: downstream action items: (1) Billing notified of potential hot-pool spill cost (2) Postmortem if impact > 30min (3) Vendor ticket for FW IO amp. I'll create the Jira.
Alex R: timeline: incident opened 09:13, mitigations rolling by 09:26, attach failures resolved by ~09:35. leaving this thread open for followups and postmortem notes.
Jin Park: I'll follow up with the rollout diff and link to the patch: https://git.redwood/infra/janitor/commit/ab12cd34
Maya Chen: saved the iostat snippet to the incident doc.
Samir: thx team. let's keep an eye on eu-west3 for the next 24h and re-evaluate scrub schedule after we get vendor analysis.
ops-bot: [RESOLVE] GPU attach timeout incidents suppressed; node iowait normalized.
Alex R: closing here unless new anomalies.
